title: Double charge on payment retries
root_cause: Check-then-insert race: pay() did SELECT to test the idempotency key then INSERT+UPDATE. Two concurrent retries of the same key both see no row and both insert and debit, charging the customer multiple times (TOCTOU, non-atomic without constraint/lock).
fix: Added UNIQUE constraint on payments(idempotency_key) and replaced SELECT-then-INSERT with atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING: if a row was inserted this request charges the account and returns True, otherwise returns False. Otherwise identical behavior single-threaded, no locks/errors surviving load.

repro_report.example_violation: idempotency violated: payment repro-key-0 was charged 8 times (8 callers returned True), must be charged exactly once

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

checks.name: agent_reproduction_test
checks.detail: the agent's own reproduction test passed 3/3 runs

fix_code:
"""Payment service with idempotency keys.

Clients retry on timeouts, so the same payment request (same idempotency key)
can arrive more than once. Each key must be charged exactly once.

The service may define MIGRATIONS, a list of SQL statements applied after
schema.sql when the database is set up.
"""
import psycopg

MIGRATIONS: list[str] = [
    "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS payments_idempotency_key_uidx ON payments (idempotency_key)",
]


def pay(conn: psycopg.Connection, idempotency_key: str, account_id: int, amount: int) -> bool:
    """Charge the account once per key. Returns True if charged, False if the key was already processed."""
    with conn.transaction():
        res = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO payments (idempotency_key, account_id, amount) VALUES (%s, %s, %s) ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING id",
            (idempotency_key, account_id, amount),
        ).fetchone()
        if res is None:
            return False
        conn.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - %s WHERE id = %s", (amount, account_id))
        return True
